title: FOGLINE devlog: zoom in on a unit and the map turns into a close-up 3D view
author: DueSpkyke
selftext:
Quick progress update on FOGLINE, my browser-based serious game about deciding under uncertainty in maritime crises. It's built as a single HTML page with an AI assistant doing most of the coding.

The big addition this week is a close-up 3D view. I took the inspiration from Falling Frontier, the sci-fi RTS by Stutter Fox Studios published by Hooded Horse. I liked how you can go from a strategic overview to watching your ships up close. In FOGLINE, when you zoom far enough on a ship or an aircraft, the 2D tactical map fades into a tilted 3D view. The models are built in code in the same "satellite watch" style as the rest of the interface. The game slows to a quarter speed while you're in it, and you can speed it back up whenever you like.

The view never shows more than you actually know. An unidentified contact stays a generic hull or a simple marker, and a submarine is only ever shown as its probability cloud. The animations replay what the game engine has already decided, so you see interceptions, misses and hits as they really happened in the simulation, not as decoration.

I also added a full sound layer: ambience, sonar pings tied to real emissions, unit replies when you select or give orders, alerts, and subtitles.

The demo video shows a destroyer in the Gulf of Aden under attack from a swarm of long-range kamikaze drones. Detection, interceptions, the one shot that misses and the damage that follows all come from the game's rules.
